https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.title: Exclusive: Hours before Huang’s reinstatement, Trump called Nvidia’s board to argue for his return
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.summary: The chipmaker’s board said it received government assurances that Huang’s return poses no national security risk.
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.author: Rohan Goswami and Shelby Talcott
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.lead_paragraph: US President Donald Trump had dialed into Nvidia’s board meeting to argue for Jensen Huang’s return, hours before the company reinstated the ousted CEO, according to people familiar with the matter.
paragraphs: US President Donald Trump had dialed into Nvidia’s board meeting to argue for Jensen Huang’s return, hours before the company reinstated the ousted CEO, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Huang, saying the company had received assurances from “senior levels of the United States government” that he posed no national security risk after carrying on an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said.

Nvidia’s board met late last night, according to a person familiar with the matter, and voted unanimously. Huang’s resignation spurred an outcry from some Silicon Valley figures who called for his return. Semafor had previously reported that a faction of directors had continued to push for him to come back.

The anti-Jensen camp was dealt a blow when they learned a leading Huang replacement candidate, Arm CEO Rene Haas, had signed a new contract with Arm extending his employment until 2033, according to another person familiar with some directors’ thinking.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” Harvey Jones, who was elevated at the time of Huang’s Nov. 12 ouster to board chairman, said in a statement.

The decision comes less than two weeks after Huang stepped down under pressure, and returns Huang to the company he founded in 1993 and built into an AI giant. Huang has also been accused of having an affair with a subordinate.
Nvidia’s stock was up nearly 30% in early trading Monday, the biggest jump in more than two decades.

https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.title: Exclusive: Commerce to add Megaspeed to trade blacklist
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.summary: US companies will not be able to sell chips to the Singapore-based firm at the heart of the Nvidia scandal without obtaining a license.
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.author: Ashley Gold
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/23/20.lead_paragraph: The Trump administration plans to add the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors, according to sources familiar with the matter.
paragraphs: The Trump administration plans to add the company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, Megaspeed, to a trade blacklist designed to prevent it from obtaining US-made semiconductors, according to sources familiar with the matter.
The Singapore-based company will be added to the Commerce Department’s entity list on Monday, the sources said.

The addition means that no US company can sell certain technologies, including semiconductors, to Megaspeed or its foreign affiliates without obtaining a license from the US government. The news comes the same day the Nvidia board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as its CEO, after President Donald Trump implored them to do so. Huang resigned less than two weeks ago amid scrutiny over his extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has been under pressure to place Megaspeed on the department’s entity list from others inside the administration, tensions that became public after news broke of Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy who was an executive at Megaspeed. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated US export controls by shipping Nvidia chips to China.

Earlier this month, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency along with the Pentagon, the State Department, and the US Trade Representative had backed putting Megaspeed on the entity list “for months” but that “Commerce holds the pen.” Bipartisan lawmakers have pressed Lutnick to put Megaspeed on the entity list and explain his decisions around Nvidia, Megaspeed, and chip export controls.

https://www.semafor.com/article/11/25/20.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/25/20.summary: “You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development,” Fouquet said on Semafor’s Future Proof.
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/25/20.author: Reed Albergotti
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/25/20.lead_paragraph: Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.
paragraphs: Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development,” Fouquet said on Semafor’s Future Proof.

The debate over Chinese access to Western technology has intensified in Washington after revelations of Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy left lawmakers divided on how aggressively to tighten curbs.

As a $520 billion de facto monopoly in chipmaking equipment, ASML sits at the center of that fight. Fouquet argued that continuing to sell China older equipment — ASML’s shipments there are more than a decade behind the cutting edge — maintains a strategic “generation gap” that keeps Beijing hooked on Western hardware rather than racing to build its own.

“For almost 30 years, we have been able to keep an extremely high market share in China — very high means close to 100% — which means that they have accepted to rely on our technology with the idea that they had access to it,” Fouquet said.
